title: The Big Wheel at z = 3.25: A Clean Galaxy-Scale Rotation Curve Disfavors a Rising MOND Acceleration Scale
description: The MOND acceleration scale a0 has been proposed to track the dark-energy density, a0 proportional to sqrt(rho_DE) (Limbach, Psaltis & Ozel 2008; Milgrom 1999) -- which makes it DECLINE at high redshift under evolving dark energy -- versus competing proposals tying a0 to the Hubble rate, a0 proportional to cH(z) (entropic/emergent gravity; quantized inertia; Modified Dark Matter), which make a0 RISE ~5x by z~3. This note confronts both with the first clean galaxy-scale probe at that epoch: THE BIG WHEEL (z=3.25, Nature Astronomy 2025, arXiv:2409.17956), an exceptionally large rotation-dominated (V/sigma~4.5) disk whose deep-MOND baryonic Tully-Fisher relation reads a0 straight off the rotation curve, a0_eff = V_circ^4/(G M_bar). With Monte-Carlo error propagation, a dynamical-mass bound on the (over-estimated) SED stellar mass, and a gas-only hard ceiling, the measured scale is a0_eff ~ 1.0-1.6e-10 m/s^2 -- its LOCAL value. The RISING branch (a0(3.25) ~ 4.6-5.9e-10, a disk spinning at 400-425 km/s) is DISFAVORED at ~2 sigma (P(a0_eff>=rise)~1-3%) (the disk spins at 280 +/- 31 km/s); a CONSTANT a0 (268-285 km/s predicted) MATCHES; the DECLINING sqrt(rho_DE) branch (246-262 km/s) is consistent, ~1 sigma low. Both coefficient footings (framework canonical a0=9.36e-11; empirical SPARC a0=1.20e-10) give the same verdict. Reported straight, single-object systematics foregrounded, and the tension with the MUSE-DARK III statistical 'rising' signal stated. HONEST SCOPE: the clean result is a NEGATIVE one -- the best high-z disk disfavors a strongly rising a0 (~2 sigma, one galaxy) and is consistent with a near-constant one, favoring the sqrt(rho_DE) reading over the cH reading -- but it does NOT confirm the framework's distinctive high-z DECLINE (which sits ~1 sigma below the measurement, within the +/-11% single-galaxy error), and is equally consistent with ordinary constant-a0 MOND. One galaxy; the a0(z) question needs a sample of clean gas-traced z~3 disks, of which the Big Wheel is the first. A data note; nothing here derives a0.
notes: A single-galaxy data-confrontation note. The Big Wheel (z=3.25) rotation curve reads a0_eff ~ 1.0-1.6e-10 (local): it EXCLUDES a rising a0 propto cH(z) at ~3-4 sigma (would need 400-425 km/s; measured 280+/-31), MATCHES constant a0 (268-285 km/s), and is CONSISTENT WITH a mildly declining a0 propto sqrt(rho_DE) (246-262 km/s, ~1 sigma low) -- but does NOT detect that decline. Both footings; systematics bounded (M_dyn caps the SED stellar mass; gas-only ceiling). In tension with MUSE-DARK III's rising signal.
